rule.statement: A carrier version selects an entire suite. There is no per-record algorithm identifier, no negotiation, and therefore nothing to downgrade.
rule.reader: A reader knows a fixed compiled-in set of (carrier, version) pairs, accepts exactly those, and refuses everything else including versions above its own.
rule.refusal: Refusal is reported and the carrier is left intact. Never skipped silently, never deleted by the read path.
rule.binding: Every carrier authenticates its own version in its associated data, so a renumbered record fails to open rather than selecting a weaker suite.
rule.label: done/<carrier>/v<suite> -- the trailing integer is the suite, not the carrier framing.

content-store-aead.why: Native and hardware-accelerated, so it adds no bundle. Forced to differ from the journal by §13.2.

local-key-envelope-aead.why: Same path, same primitive; L_local is a non-extractable AES-GCM CryptoKey (§13.3).

network-envelope-aead.why: Named here so the suite is complete. Its wire format is row 4 and review 3b.

journal-aead.provider: audited RustCrypto chacha20poly1305 crate, compiled to an inlined wasm module (wasm/journal-seal), instantiated synchronously
journal-aead.why: Selected by row 2. The only primitive the platform does not supply, and the only one on the crash path.

subkey-derivation.why: Derivation happens once at open, where async is free. Labels are what keep §13.2 separation real.

mutation-signature.why: Small, fast, widely reviewed. Availability is now broad enough that the fallback path §13.10 anticipated is a compatibility question, not a design one.

account-credential-signature.also_accepted: Ed25519, already selected above for mutation-signature
account-credential-signature.why: Selected by row 12, and the one role this suite does not choose: WebAuthn credential creation is a negotiation and the authenticator picks from the offered list. The offer is [-8 Ed25519, -7 ES256] and is frozen at creation inside a service-signed binding, so nothing renegotiates afterwards. ES256 is the addition; it meets §13.10's criteria and is async-path only, so §13.2 is untouched. No KAT here: its verification is exercised end to end by row 12's vectors, whose keypair checks its own halves.

public-key-wrap.primitive: HPKE base mode, DHKEM(X25519, HKDF-SHA256) / HKDF-SHA256 / AES-256-GCM
public-key-wrap.why: RFC 9180 with the most widely implemented ciphersuite. Covers the R_pub and per-reader wrap cases uniformly (§13.2).

credential-stretching.why: Selected by rows 13 and 14, and §13.10 answers it as one row for both: the recovery code and the device-lock code are generated at 125 bits, so the entropy deficit a work factor exists to cover does not exist. It rests on the invariant that such a code is never user-chosen, user-extended or truncated (§13.10).

slot-verifier-stretching.why: Selected by row 12, on a stronger argument than the two above: the verifier checks a signature rather than a secret, so there is no secret in the profile to grind (§13.9).

hash.why: One hash everywhere HKDF, signatures and commitments need one.

carriers.name: journal-entry
carriers.encoding: the "2:" string prefix on the localStorage value
carriers.label: done/jrnl/v1
carriers.note: Version 2 under suite 1 is not an inconsistency. The leading integer is the carrier framing, which counted from 1 when the journal was plaintext; the trailing v1 in the label is the suite. §4 of the row 1 document explains why both axes exist.

carriers.name: network-envelope
carriers.label: done/env/v1
carriers.note: This row read "unselected" for as long as row 4 was open, and stayed that way after row 4 closed. The registry is the suite's inventory of every carrier, so an entry that is stale in the safe-looking direction is the one worth guarding: `checkCarriers` lets a null suite through on the strength of a named owner, which is exactly what a closed row no longer needs.

acceptance.why: The only version this suite defines.
No version 0 was ever written. A record claiming one is malformed or hostile.
Above what this reader knows. A newer writer touched this store; guessing at its framing is how a store gets corrupted.
A plaintext entry from a pre-encryption build. Replaying it means shipping a plaintext reader, which §6.1 forbids and §11.1 tests for.
The only version this suite defines.
Above what this reader knows. Refusing a key envelope closes the workspace; opening it wrongly loses it.
The only version this suite defines.
No version 0 was ever minted. The relay validates the clear header (§7.2), so a malformed version is refused before any content key is involved.
Above what this reader knows. Row 4 binds `v` in both the AAD and the signature, so a receiver that guessed at a newer framing would be authenticating bytes it cannot parse.

async: HPKE base mode, DHKEM(X25519, HKDF-SHA256) / HKDF-SHA256 / AES-256-GCM
